title: Redwood November 2026 Leadership Update
summary: Quarterly leadership update focused on Q4 priorities: product roadmap (Dedicated and Private launches), operational reliability, hiring posture, and GTM motions. Brief financial/metrics update, security/compliance milestone recap, and a Q&A. Action items assigned for follow-ups on sales enablement, benchmarking, and hiring timelines.
next_steps: Priya to share updated product roadmap deck by 2026-11-09
Maya to distribute enterprise pitch kit and pricing FAQ by 2026-11-06
Liam to publish incident postmortem and action plan to #ops by 2026-11-05
People team to open hiring requisitions for infra SREs and senior backend by 2026-11-10
action_items: Owner: Priya Nair - Update roadmap deck (include Dedicated launch contingency) - Due: 2026-11-09
Owner: Liam Chen - Incident postmortem and SLO remediation plan - Due: 2026-11-05
Owner: Maya Rodriguez - Enterprise pitch kit and pricing FAQ - Due: 2026-11-06
Owner: Noah Patel - Run and share benchmark results for quantized 4-bit models on Dedicated for reference - Due: 2026-11-12
Owner: Sofia Alvarez - Hiring requisitions and interview panel setup - Due: 2026-11-10
transcript:
[00:00] Ava Morgan: Hey everyone, thanks for joining this morning. Quick check — can you see my slides? Uh, looks like yes. Welcome to our November leadership update, we'll try to keep to an hour.
[00:18] Ethan Park: Morning all. Quick agenda: product roadmap, reliability review, hiring, GTM, then Q and A.
[00:30] Priya Nair: I'll kick off with product. So, Q4 priorities — Dedicated GA cadence is the big milestone. We're targeting an initial fleet for customers mid-November, with a soft roll to select accounts. There's a contingency window in case the autoscaler needs another validation pass.
[00:50] Liam Chen: To add, the autoscaler hit a throttle edge case in the last stress run — long story short, the control plane didn't reclaim idle capacity fast enough. We have a patch lined up, and we'll run a replay on staging tomorrow.
[01:06] Maya Rodriguez: From sales' perspective, timing matters a lot — our enterprise leads want deterministic throughput and SLOs. If Dedicated GA slips beyond late November, we'll need to offer extended pilots on Hosted with stronger SLAs, which impacts margins.
[01:26] Ava Morgan: Understood. Priya, can we build a comms plan for customers if GA moves?
[01:32] Priya Nair: Yep, I can draft messaging and a few rollback/fallback options. We'll share by the end of next week.
[01:40] [00:60] Noah Patel: I ran the quantization experiments — 4-bit quant with the new kernel set yields about 1.9x throughput for our baseline LLM on the 80GB A100 class in Dedicated sim. There's some perplexity variance on long-tail prompts; we're adding a small calibration layer.
[02:05] Liam Chen: That's promising. Noah, can you push a perf summary to the benchmarks doc and include the sample prompts where we saw regressions?
[02:12] Noah Patel: Yep, I'll drop that into the shared sheet after this.
[02:18] Priya Nair: On Private deployment — we've got two customers in final legal review. The VPC onboarding flow needs a couple UX touch ups: key rotation UX and KMS integration steps were confusing to non-infra folks during the last pilot.
[02:34] Ethan Park: Also a note on orchestration: our config layer needs clearer defaults for private, otherwise operators manually tweak kernel flags and that causes inconsistent perf.
[02:45] Ava Morgan: Good call. Product and engineering to align on default profiles for Private.
[02:50] [03:00] Sofia Alvarez: Hiring update — we're green-lit for 6 infra hires and 4 PM/SDR roles this quarter. We need to prioritize SRE and senior infra engineers; candidate pipeline is thin in EMEA but better in NA.
[03:15] Maya Rodriguez: Sales will coordinate for referral bonuses — we have a few inbound folks from customer references.
[03:20] [03:30] Ava Morgan: Financial brief — revenue growth for the quarter is on track at 34% QoQ, gross margins improved slightly due to caching and batching improvements. Our burn rate improved because of Dedicated bookings converting to reserved capacity.
[03:42] Priya Nair: A quick product note: Redwood Optimize shipped the first iteration of model recommendations — initial customers saw up to 18% cost reduction with no user-visible latency change. We need to scale the telemetry for more automated suggestions.
[04:00] Liam Chen: Ops — we had a P1 on Oct 22 related to KV cache invalidation, which caused tail latency spikes for about 18 minutes. Root cause: cache invalidation race on concurrent rollouts. We've put a guard in the rollout pipeline; full fix requires a small API change.
[04:22] Ava Morgan: Thanks. How many customers noticed impact?
[04:25] Liam Chen: Two customers with high-traffic routes reported errors; our mitigation worked, but we need to be proactive.
[04:30] Maya Rodriguez: We did reach out to the accounts and offered credits; they were appreciative but asked for a postmortem.
[04:36] Ava Morgan: Make sure we share the postmortem with the account teams and the customers.
[04:40] [05:00] Ethan Park: Security/compliance — SOC 2 readiness is on track, auditor kickoff next week. On Private, we've completed initial KMS integration tests and policy-based RBAC for control plane ops. Still working through a couple of logging retention edge cases for customers in EMEA.
[05:20] Priya Nair: Also, legal flagged a data residency question for a prospect in Germany; we need to make sure our region map and export controls docs are synced.
[05:30] Ava Morgan: Noted. Priya, coordinate with Legal to update the public docs.
[05:36] [06:00] Maya Rodriguez: GTM update — enterprise pipeline grew 22% this quarter; our conversion time tightened a bit but enterprise deals still require SSO, audit logs, and a Private or Dedicated option to close. We're seeing comparisons to Anthropic and OpenAI for price/perf and to NVIDIA for on-prem inference stacks.
[06:18] Noah Patel: On benchmarks — we should publish a transparent benchmarks page showing latency/cost tradeoffs across Hosted, Dedicated, and Private; customers often ask for apples-to-apples. We need to include quantized variants and sequence-length assumptions.
[06:34] Priya Nair: Agreed. I'll own a baseline doc and coordinate with Noah and Liam for test artifacts.
[06:40] [07:00] Ava Morgan: Ok let's open the floor for questions. Please be concise.
[07:05] Speaker 1 (from Eng): Hey, quick on SRE hiring — do we have interview loops defined?
[07:10] Sofia Alvarez: Yes, we standardized an SRE loop: system design, behavioral, and a debugging pair session. We'll publish the rubric later today.
[07:18] Speaker 2 (Sales): For pricing FAQs, can we get a short note on how Dedicated pricing compares to Hosted and what the reserved commit looks like?
[07:25] Maya Rodriguez: We'll create a simple one-pager and a spreadsheet example showing unit economics.
[07:30] [08:00] Speaker 3 (Support): On the incident postmortem, can we include the exact kube rollout steps that triggered the race? Ops asked for that detail.
[08:06] Liam Chen: Yep; technical appendix will include the rollout sequence and suggested mitigations.
[08:12] Ava Morgan: Any more? If not, quick recap.
[08:16] [09:00] Priya Nair: Recap from product: Dedicated GA targeted mid-Nov, contingency plan and comms by 2026-11-09. Private onboarding UX fixes next sprint; default profiles for private to be defined.
[09:30] Liam Chen: Ops recap: postmortem due 2026-11-05, autoscaler patch deploy and staging replay tomorrow morning.
[09:45] Maya Rodriguez: GTM recap: enterprise kit and pricing FAQ by 2026-11-06, start account outreach for pilot expansions.
[10:00] Sofia Alvarez: Hiring recap: requisitions live by 2026-11-10, interview rubrics published today.
[10:12] Ava Morgan: Great. Two final asks: one, let's keep comms tight to customers — if anyone hears customer anxiety, escalate to Maya. Two, prioritize the reliability fixes even if it nudges feature timelines — reliability first.
[10:30] [11:00] Priya Nair: Noted. Thanks everyone. We'll follow up with the deck and links.
[11:06] Ava Morgan: Thanks team, meeting adjourned.
[11:10] [END]
